prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: parking lot collision in Pasadena, Texas. Injury: back strain. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1282; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record for this part. You can use the name listed on the case caption.

Q: Understood. Where were you on the day of the collision?
A: I was in a grocery store parking lot in Pasadena, Texas. I had just loaded bags into the trunk of my car.

Q: Describe your vehicle's position and the other vehicle's movement.
A: I was parked in a row near the store entrance, backing out slowly. The other driver came down the aisle fast and clipped the rear quarter panel of my car. I felt a hard jolt and the car rocked.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the impact?
A: Not really. I heard an engine revving and then I saw it at the last second. I had already started moving, so I couldn't stop in time.

Q: Did you feel any pain immediately afterward?
A: Not right away. I got out, looked at the bumper, and went back to my seat. About an hour later my lower back started to tighten up, and by evening it was sharp when I bent over.

Q: Did you seek medical care?
A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic the next morning. They diagnosed a back strain and gave me muscle relaxers and a referral to physical therapy.

Q: How often have you attended physical therapy?
A: I've been going about twice a week. Some sessions help, and some days I'm still sore afterward.

Q: Have you missed any work because of the injury?
A: I've been on modified duties. I can't lift heavy boxes anymore, so I've had to ask a coworker to help with those tasks.

Q: How has the injury affected your everyday activities?
A: Simple things take longer. Putting on socks, vacuuming, or sitting through a long drive are harder than they used to be. I've stopped playing in my weekend recreational league because I can't twist the way I need to.

Q: Have you had any prior back problems?
A: I had some stiffness years ago after a fall at work, but it resolved and I didn't need treatment for it.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add about how the collision has affected you?
A: Mostly that I'm frustrated. I was careful that day, and now I'm dealing with pain that changes my routine every week.
